# Active work

This is the durable, human-readable resumption queue. Detailed designs remain in their
linked roadmap documents. Follow
`skills/agent/record-user-directed-work/SKILL.md` before implementing substantive user
direction. Check an item only when its evidence is
recorded; Git preserves prior states.

**Current development release: 1.4.0.** The latest published release is 1.3.1.
[`release-goals.json`](release-goals.json) retains the 1.3.1 patch program and
its explicitly carried-forward 1.4 obligations. [RELEASE-INTEGRATION-004](#release-integration-004-reconcile-and-execute-the-13-release-backlog)
and the [1.3 integration plan](1.3-integration.md) are retained as 1.3.0 history.
Existing unchecked acceptance remains open; evidence from an older release does not
establish readiness for either the patch line or 1.4.0.

**Maintainer approvals, 2026-09-13:** ADR 0011 is accepted for 1.1, including
opt-in `literate-markdown@2` domain metadata and typed acceptance while preserving
`@1`. The Rust regression boundary in the reviewed
`_build/rs-dev/_build/rust-proof/REVIEW.md` is accepted for promotion: one public
`checked_sum(i64, i64) -> Option<i64>`, `None` on signed overflow, no I/O/state,
and all Cargo targets required. Live release gates for 0.8.4 and remaining 1.1
qualification are authorized with the configured coding CLI/model, including
generation, compilation and execution in test workspaces, installed-project tests,
sample rebuilds and live receipts. These approvals do not authorize new services
or accounts, establish passing qualification, or acknowledge source retirement.

## Historical release context

**Break-glass (2026-08-28, not durable SemVer advice):** `0.8.0` is still a
minor *number* because no `1.0.0` has shipped and the work has lived on minors
and patches. For this cut only, treat every remaining open `[ ]` and `[~]`
queue item on `main` as 0.8.0 in-scope **including breaking changes**, as if
this were the first major. Per-item historical `Release target:` lines that
name `0.3.1`, `0.4.1`, `after 0.8.0`, or `not 0.8.0 product` are superseded
until `v0.8.0` is tagged. Do not copy this into `release-project` or
`docs/architecture/project-releases.md`. [RELEASE-013](#release-013-agent-owned-patch-content-remaining-proc-kill-call-sites-as-073)
stays a `0.7.3` patch on `release/0.7.x`; do not merge that line into `main`.
Obsolete land-as-is artifacts (TEST-CACHE-001 WIP `c0439340`, older-line
backport worktrees) stay obsolete. There is no framework rule against IDEs or
complete applications; [IDE-001](#x-ide-001-evaluate-a-provider-neutral-specification-led-ide-sample-catalog)
withdrew that prohibition.

**0.10.0 headline:** operator adoption. See
[ADOPTION-001](#x-adoption-001-make-operator-adoption-the-post-090-product-headline)
and the [operator adoption program](operator-adoption.md). `v0.9.0` is
tagged. STATUS-001, ONBOARD-001, GOLDEN-PATH-001, and BROWNFIELD-STATE-001
are eligible on this line. [QUEUE-HYGIENE-001](#x-queue-hygiene-001-archive-completed-queue-items-and-reconcile-the-open-tracker)
is closed.

### [ ] INIT-CONVERT-FORCE-001 — Add an explicit re-init escape hatch for already-initialized projects

- **Priority:** P2 (not onboard; not 0.9.0 product)
- **Release target:** 1.1.0
- **Previous release target:** after published v0.9.0 unless RELEASE-0.9-CUT-001 promotes it
- **GitHub issue:** [#301](https://github.com/NVIDIA-dev/literate-ai/issues/301)
- **Owner:** litai init --convert collision handling
- **Direction:** Already-initialized projects cannot re-run init --convert; update is the only path,
      and operators need a reviewed reset when incremental update is stuck.
- **Conclusion:** Add a fail-closed --force (or equivalent) that re-runs convert against an
      initialized tree only with explicit acknowledgement. Do not fold this into onboard.
- **Depends on:** RELEASE-0.9-CUT-001
- **Next action:** After v0.9.0, specify the acknowledged re-init flag. Do not implement it inside onboard.
- **Implementation:**
  - [ ] Add an explicit re-init flag that refuses to run without acknowledgement
  - [ ] Preserve Gitlink and nonempty-tree blockers unless the flag names them
  - [ ] Keep onboard pointing at this item rather than absorbing the flag
- **Evidence:**
  - [ ] Public-API tests cover refusal without the flag and acknowledged re-init
  - [ ] ONBOARD-001 still cites this as related re-init scope, not the onboard verb

### [ ] WORKER-GIT-CRED-001 — Broker short-lived Git source credentials for dynamic workers

- **Priority:** P2 (1.0 worker fleet; not 0.9.0 product)
- **Release target:** 1.1.0
- **Previous release target:** 1.0; after published v0.9.0
- **GitHub issue:** [#286](https://github.com/NVIDIA-dev/literate-ai/issues/286)
- **Owner:** worker source materialization and forge credential brokerage
- **Direction:** Workers must fetch an exact Git revision, but the contract assumes the worker can
      already authenticate to the forge. Ephemeral fleets cannot share a long-lived PAT or a
      permanent SSH key per host.
- **Conclusion:** Add a provider-neutral short-lived Git credential contract for worker-to-forge
      fetch, submodules, and Git LFS. Keep credentials out of project authority and the persistent
      worker catalog. Distinct from controller-to-worker SSH.
- **Depends on:** RELEASE-0.9-CUT-001
- **Next action:** `literate_ai.security.worker_forge_credentials` lands the contract, the
      GitHub App and GitLab CI adapters, and the `GIT_ASKPASS`-based fetch/submodule/LFS
      wiring. Still open: an external OIDC/workload-identity broker adapter, a generic
      command-provider adapter, and wiring this module into the live worker dispatch
      pipeline (`execution_dispatch.py`) so a real dynamic worker invokes it instead of
      `source_materialization.py`'s already-authenticated-worker assumption.
- **Implementation:**
  - [x] Define a short-lived worker-to-forge credential contract and lifetime
  - [x] Support at least GitHub App installation tokens and GitLab CI job tokens
  - [x] Refuse to persist credentials in project authority or worker catalog files
  - [ ] Add the external OIDC/workload-identity broker and generic command-provider adapters
  - [ ] Wire the contract into the live worker dispatch/fetch pipeline
- **Evidence:**
  - [x] Focused tests cover acquisition, use during fetch, and expiry without catalog writes
        (`tests/critical/test_worker_forge_credentials.py`)
  - [ ] Controller-to-worker SSH stays a separate credential class

### [ ] SUBMODULE-ORCH-001 — Orchestrate Git-submodule virtual monorepos without flattening Gitlinks

- **Priority:** P1 (brownfield; distinct from the Gitlink block)
- **Release target:** 1.1.0 (current tracker milestone; design accepted)
- **Design review:** [ADR 0039](../decisions/0039-1.1-capability-boundaries.md), Accepted by explicit maintainer approval.
- **GitHub issue:** [#279](https://github.com/NVIDIA-dev/literate-ai/issues/279)
- **Owner:** init convert orchestration and Gitlink preservation
- **Direction:** Convert correctly blocks nested submodules, but a virtual monorepo that should keep
      independently owned Gitlinks has no supported orchestration path.
- **Conclusion:** Add a supported orchestration path that preserves child Gitlinks and does not
      flatten them at convert time. Distinct from CONVERSION-GITLINK-001 (block) and
      BROWNFIELD-STATE-001 (authority stages). Root authority owns exact repository
      pins and explicitly declared cross-project relationships, not copies of child
      Components or a replacement for each child's independent release authority.
      Issue #279's seven acceptance criteria and Accepted ADR 0039 remain the full
      scope; a read-only inventory or successful scaffold alone cannot close it.
- **Depends on:** RELEASE-0.9-CUT-001, CONVERSION-GITLINK-001
- **Lifecycle delivery:** A root must delegate build, package and container operations
      to independent children through an explicit command contract. Metadata validation
      alone does not deliver this. Implement an inventory-complete, target-specific
      dependency plan and acknowledged executor with logs, failure propagation and
      artifact-verified recovery. Keep Git refresh on the existing transactional path;
      never disguise a shell Git update as coherent authority refresh. Work is tracked
      by #279; native SDK admission and Component worker transport remain owned by
      #407 and #403 respectively, and are not prerequisites for delegating retained
      child build commands on one supported worker.
      Child receipts must accumulate elapsed time across the command sequence,
      including failures and interruptions. Keep LFS test pointers canonical LF
      on every host; platform newline translation must not weaken the verifier.
      - [ ] Qualify a real independent-child dependency chain through the public CLI.
      - [ ] Refuse missing children, unsupported operations, stale pins and cycles before execution.
      - [ ] Preserve diagnostics and terminate descendants on failure or cancellation.
      - [ ] Verify exact artifact bytes before resuming successful child operations.

### [~] SAMPLE-TOOLCHAIN-DEMAND-001 — Discover compilers only for selected variants

- **Priority:** P0 (a selected non-C++ native-worker portfolio fails before generation
      when the host correctly omits the unselected `lang-cpp` toolchain)
- **Release target:** 1.1.0
- **Previous release target:** 0.9.0
- **GitHub issue:** [#303](https://github.com/NVIDIA-dev/literate-ai/issues/303)
- **Observed behavior:** Exact NVIDIA Windows run `20260904T055433Z-b46b04b8`
      materializes the clean candidate and then fails in `run_all()` at unconditional
      `discover_cpp_toolchain()`, before `durable-split-service` reaches `run_sample()`.
      The CPU worker masks this boundary violation because it already has a compiler.
- **Expected behavior:** Sample execution discovers only toolchains demanded by the
      selected Component/Flavor variants; a Python/JavaScript portfolio does not require
      `lang-cpp` or a compiler from `os-base`.
- **Conclusion:** The top-level eager discovery is a second, obsolete universal-
      toolchain authority. Remove it and retain discovery in the existing C++ execution
      branch, where missing C++ remains a hard failure for an actually selected C++
      variant.
- **Competing hypotheses:** A worker misconfiguration cannot explain why an unselected
      compiler is queried. Adding C++ to `os-base` contradicts ADR 0033 and would mask
      the invalid dependency edge. The durable Standard branch does not consume the
      optional host-E2E C++ toolchain.
- **Falsification:** The theory is wrong if forbidding C++ discovery still prevents the
      selected durable sample from entering execution, or the repaired native run later
      reaches a legitimate durable operation that selects `lang-cpp`.
- **Implementation:**
  - [x] Remove top-level C++ discovery and pass no shared compiler into selected sample
        execution; the C++ host-E2E variant retains its local discovery fallback.
  - [x] Add a regression that forbids C++ discovery across an aggregate containing the
        durable portfolio while preserving the normal report contract.
- **Evidence:**
  - [x] Focused regression and complete sample-ladder module pass: 89 tests with 6
        capability skips.
  - [x] Uninterrupted Python gate from test one: 3,372 tests pass with 30
        capability skips in 1,378.358 seconds.
  - [ ] The exact NVIDIA Windows durable portfolio passes on the compiler-free host.

### [~] HOST-CODEX-PACKAGE-001 — Install the complete Codex runtime closure

- **Priority:** P0 (the managed Windows Codex executable exits successfully but cannot
      write files because its required code-mode host was not installed)
- **Release target:** 1.1.0
- **Previous release target:** 0.9.0
- **GitHub issue:** [#302](https://github.com/NVIDIA-dev/literate-ai/issues/302)
- **Observed behavior:** The NVIDIA Windows fan-out selected the exact managed Codex
      executable installed from the declared standalone archive. Live model preflight
      then returned zero without a response file and diagnosed a missing adjacent
      `codex-code-mode-host.exe`. The same account, model, task, and host succeeded with
      the system Codex package, which includes that companion executable.
- **Expected behavior:** Managed coding-agent artifacts provide and verify their entire
      required runtime closure while exposing only their declared executable directory
      on `PATH`.
- **Conclusion:** The official standalone Codex asset is not a complete installation for
      file-writing code-mode tasks. Every supported host tuple must consume the official
      `codex-package-*` asset, declare its runtime companions, preserve their directory
      topology, and invalidate an installation when a required companion disappears.
      The generic artifact contract—not Codex-specific installer code—owns these rules.
- **Competing hypotheses:** Authentication, model availability, SSH transport, and the
      task itself are contradicted by the system package succeeding on the same worker.
      An unreported nonzero process failure is contradicted by the captured zero exit and
      explicit missing-host diagnostic.
- **Falsification:** The theory is wrong if the official package is installed with every
      declared companion intact and the same exact live preflight still reports the host
      missing or fails before producing its response file.
- **Implementation:**
  - [x] Extend managed-artifact SBOM parsing with safe, duplicate-free required runtime
        paths and verify those paths whenever an installed manifest is reused.
  - [x] Normalize the primary executable within the first declared `PATH` directory so
        package-relative companion lookup remains intact.
  - [x] Pin the official package URL and digest for all five supported OS/CPU tuples in
        both framework and project-template SBOMs.
- **Evidence:**
  - [x] Package fixture coverage proves the primary executable and adjacent host remain
        in `bin`, and deleting the host invalidates the managed installation.
  - [x] Strict CycloneDX parsing and tuple-level regressions require all five Codex
        realizations to select package assets and declare their code-mode host.
  - [x] The uninterrupted final-code local Python gate passes all 3,372 tests with 30
        expected skips after lifecycle-driver and documentation authority review.
  - [ ] The exact NVIDIA Windows worker installs the new package and completes live
        model preflight plus the durable split-service portfolio.
  - [ ] The exact hosted release gates pass.

### [x] RELEASE-0.9-DEFECTS-009 — Preserve native Windows fan-out command dispatch

- **Priority:** P0 (both private Windows release workers fail before exact source
      checkout or generation)
- **Release target:** 0.9.0
- **GitHub issue:** [#284](https://github.com/NVIDIA-dev/literate-ai/issues/284)
- **Owner:** remote sample fan-out SSH transport boundary
- **Observed behavior:** Exact Git-backed `durable-split-service` fan-out reaches both
      Windows 11 workers, but PowerShell reports that `bash` is not recognized. The
      controller has already constructed an encoded PowerShell receiver and then wraps
      it in `bash -lic` through its local `_ssh_arguments()` shim.
- **Conclusion:** Windows workers are not required to install Bash. The shared SSH
      adapter has carried an explicit `login_shell=False` native-Windows contract since
      `25bc2666`, and hardware probing applies it successfully. Fan-out predates that
      parameter and drops both the platform shell choice and the worker's configured
      SSH-compatible transport. Route every fan-out SSH operation through the worker's
      platform and transport while retaining `bash -lic` for POSIX PATH discovery.
- **Competing hypotheses:** Authentication and DNS are contradicted by current typed
      probes and successful raw native PowerShell on both hosts. An invalid encoded
      payload is contradicted because the wrapper fails while resolving `bash`, before
      PowerShell receives it. Installing Git Bash would mask the violated Windows
      contract and add an undeclared prerequisite.
- **Falsification:** If the unchanged encoded receiver fails when sent directly through
      the same SSH endpoint, or if fan-out still emits `bash -lic` after platform-aware
      argument projection, this theory is wrong.
- **Implementation:**
  - [x] Carry the complete Worker into fan-out SSH argument projection, use its declared
        transport, and disable login-shell wrapping only for Windows.
  - [x] Apply the same projection to Git-source execution, working-tree staging and
        execution, and post-run workspace probing.
- **Evidence:**
  - [x] Both independent Windows endpoints return `LITAI_NATIVE_OK` for a raw
        noninteractive PowerShell command sent without Bash.
  - [x] Focused contracts pass and content-addressed working-tree runs on both Windows
        workers advance beyond remote shell dispatch and bootstrap. Git-mode source
        checkout is independently blocked by the deferred credential lifecycle in
        #286, not by Windows command projection.

### [x] RELEASE-0.9-DEFECTS-010 — Make coding agents part of the universal OS toolchain

- **Priority:** P0 (a reachable worker can pass bootstrap and fail only when the
      explicitly selected coding agent is invoked)
- **Release target:** 0.9.0
- **GitHub issue:** [#285](https://github.com/NVIDIA-dev/literate-ai/issues/285)
- **Owner:** `os-base` and `os-*` Flavor authority, host installer, and remote-worker
      bootstrap
- **Owning ADR:** [ADR 0033](../decisions/0033-os-base-universal-toolchain.md)
- **Observed behavior:** Native `make install` SBOMs declare Python, Git, and Git LFS,
      while `detect-before-install` separately hardcodes Node, build tools, and a
      one-of coding-agent probe. The Windows NVIDIA worker therefore completed native
      PowerShell dispatch and framework setup, then failed because the controller's
      explicit `codex` selection was absent.
- **Conclusion:** Coding agents are toolchains. Make `os-base` own universal logical
      capabilities and their provider alternatives; make each concrete OS Flavor own
      only native package names, manager commands, and exact OS/architecture artifact
      realizations. Both installation entrypoints compose those same documents.
      Explicit `CODING_CLI` selection must be exact; when none is explicit, any
      installed supported provider satisfies the group and the declared default is
      installed only if the group is empty. Authentication remains separate state.
- **Competing hypotheses:** A worker-only Codex install would clear this one symptom
      but leaves the same failure for Claude, Cursor Agent, or OpenCode. Treating all
      providers as mandatory would waste host state and contradict the existing
      provider-selection contract; the invariant is one exact selected realization,
      not simultaneous authentication to every service.
- **Falsification:** If both install paths already consume one declarative capability
      source, or a worker with an explicit absent provider is rejected or provisioned
      before generation, the duplicate-authority theory is wrong.
- **Implementation:**
  - [x] Add the `os-base` Flavor and logical CycloneDX toolchain SBOM; keep language,
        build, accelerator, and authentication requirements outside it.
  - [x] Move tuple realization SBOMs beneath their owning `os-*` Flavors and compose
        base capability semantics with exact OS/CPU/GPU package or artifact details.
  - [x] Make `make install` and `detect-before-install` use the same parser, probes,
        consent boundary, selected-provider install, and unsupported-tuple inventory.
  - [x] Pass the controller's exact coding-agent selection into remote bootstrap and
        retain executable/path evidence before generation.
- **Evidence:**
  - [x] Contract tests cover base/OS closure, all four providers, explicit selection,
        default selection, decline, install/re-probe, archive integrity and traversal,
        unsupported tuples, and no credential mutation.
  - [x] macOS, Debian Linux, native Windows CPU, and native Windows NVIDIA runs prove
        preflight selects or provisions the requested provider before generation.
        Both Windows hosts now pass base plus selected JavaScript/Make bootstrap and
        reach live model resolution; after host authentication was repaired, the
        native Windows NVIDIA worker provisioned the managed Codex runtime and passed
        the complete durable portfolio.
  - [x] The CPU build exposed a final platform-path edge: generated Make recipes used
        an unquoted `$(LITAI_LANGUAGE_TOOL)`, splitting the manager-proven
        `C:\\Program Files\\nodejs\\node.exe` path. A direct GnuWin32 Make/Git Bash
        experiment proves `"$(LITAI_LANGUAGE_TOOL)"` succeeds. Skill version 1.6.2 now
        requires that exact form, and deterministic Python admission rejects the
        unquoted form before spending a builder repair cycle.

### [x] RELEASE-0.9-DEFECTS-011 — Close temporary SQLite fixtures on Windows

- **Priority:** P0 (the exact Windows CI shard fails after 1,255 passing tests)
- **Release target:** 0.9.0
- **GitHub issue:** [#287](https://github.com/NVIDIA-dev/literate-ai/issues/287)
- **Observed behavior:** Four durable schema contract tests finish their assertions,
      then Windows rejects `TemporaryDirectory` cleanup with sharing violation 32 for
      each fixture's unique `cache.sqlite3` file.
- **Conclusion:** `sqlite3.Connection.__exit__` commits or rolls back the transaction;
      it does not close the connection. The test-local reference therefore remains
      live during directory cleanup. POSIX unlink semantics mask the leak. Close every
      fixture connection explicitly while retaining transaction boundaries; do not add
      sleeps, retries, or ignored cleanup errors.
- **Evidence:**
  - [x] Exact CI run `33804871632` records four identical Windows sharing violations
        and no assertion failures; 1,255 adjacent tests pass.
  - [x] A minimal native Windows control reproduces the locked file immediately after
        connection context exit, while explicit `close()` releases it.
  - [x] All 16 durable portfolio contracts and Ruff checks pass after deterministic
        closure; production schema inspection already closes in `finally`. The
        uninterrupted local gate then passes 3,341 tests with 30 expected skips.
  - [x] Exact run `33836023512` passes all three native Windows test shards.

### [ ] IPC-SURFACE-001 — Unified IPC-surface contract with MCP/REST/gRPC adapters

- **Priority:** P1 (toolbox gap: MCP is taught but its peers REST and gRPC are
      not; the ADR-0027 frontend→API boundary has no described, versioned,
      conformance-tested contract)
- **Release target:** 1.1.0
- **Previous release target:** 0.9.0 (feature; lands on `main`)
- **Reopened during 1.1 reconciliation:** unchecked acceptance remains below.
- **Owning ADR:** [ADR 0029](../decisions/0029-ipc-surface-contract.md)
      (Accepted 2026-09-01 after planning-cycle review; scheduled for 0.9.0)
- **Direction:** Introduce one protocol-neutral "IPC surface" notion — a declared
      schema (schema-validated input, typed output, structured errors), a served
      self-description at a discoverable path, a verifier-owned conformance
      acceptance oracle (built on the ADR-0028 acceptance shape + the shipped
      `--litai-serve` launch), and a semantic-version compatibility promise reusing
      ADR-0005's machinery. Make `mcp-application` the first adapter and add
      `rest-application` (OpenAPI/JSON-Schema) and `grpc-application`
      (`.proto` + reflection) adapters under a shared parent. The served
      self-description is the always-current, conformance-checked API
      documentation. GraphQL and a schema-source Flavor are anticipated follow-ons,
      out of the first pass.
- **Depends on:** ADR 0005 (public interface + compatibility promise),
      ADR 0026 (deployment unit that exposes a surface), ADR 0028 (verifier-owned
      acceptance pattern), the shipped `--litai-serve` launch (#214).
- **Progress (2026-09-01):** landed. Core (37498f9a):
      `IpcSurfaceConformanceAcceptance` (`ipc-surface-conformance-acceptance@1`) —
      protocol-neutral oracle (open `protocol` tag, `description_probe`,
      `declared_schema_identity`, response-validating `request_cases`,
      `surface_version` + reused `CompatibilityPromise`); engine-free
      `decide_ipc_surface_conformance` split from an `IpcSurfaceProbe` port;
      `resolve_component_acceptance_oracle` loads the IPC oracle when a
      persistent-service verifier document declares the IPC schema (else the plain
      service probe); `_accept_ipc_surface_conformance` launches via
      `--litai-serve`, fetches the served description, decides, binds evidence.
      Adapters (ee6af0bd): `rest-application` (OpenAPI/JSON-Schema, `/openapi.json`,
      protocol `rest`), `grpc-application` (`.proto` + reflection, protocol
      `grpc`), and `mcp-application` re-framed as the first adapter (with the full
      digest cascade re-pinned).
- **Evidence:**
  - [x] ADR 0029 accepted through a planning cycle before implementation
        (accepted 2026-09-01; targeted at 0.9.0).
  - [x] A conformance oracle fails a surface whose served description does not
        match its declared schema, or whose response does not validate
        (`decide_ipc_surface_conformance`; `test_ipc_surface_acceptance.py`
        `description_mismatch` / `response_invalid` / `description_missing`).
  - [x] `rest-application` and `grpc-application` adapters ship under the shared
        parent; `mcp-application` is re-framed as the first adapter.
  - [ ] Live confirmation that a *generated* REST/gRPC surface serves a matching
        self-description and passes the oracle end-to-end (needs live generation;
        the offline tests prove the decision/loader/dispatch, not a generated
        surface).

### [ ] ACCEPTANCE-SERVICE-002 — Persistent-service EXECUTE launches one-shot, not a listening server

- **Priority:** P1 (follow-on to #213; the service oracle runs but can never pass)
- **Release target:** 1.1.0
- **Previous release target:** 0.8.2 or next minor (needs a service-launch command mode)
- **Reopened during 1.1 reconciliation:** unchecked acceptance remains below.
- **GitHub issue:** [#214](https://github.com/NVIDIA-dev/literate-ai/issues/214)
- **Owner:** `src/literate_ai/adapters/standard_project.py` (`_runtime_command`),
      `src/literate_ai/adapters/lifecycle/standard_local.py`
      (`_accept_persistent_service` command build ~2494)
- **Direction:** With ACCEPTANCE-SERVICE-001 (#213) fixed, a `persistent-service`
      Component now dispatches to `_accept_persistent_service`, which starts the
      artifact and polls `{base_url}/health`. But it always fails
      `persistent-service exited before acceptance completed`: the EXECUTE argv
      comes from `_runtime_command(..., phase=EXECUTE)` which is one-shot
      `--litai-smoke` mode for every entrypoint kind, so the artifact handles one
      invocation, prints one JSON response, and exits rc=0 instead of binding a
      port and serving.
- **Conclusion:** The persistent-service acceptance must launch the artifact in a
      *server* mode, not the one-shot smoke mode. Add a service-launch command
      variant (e.g. a `--litai-serve` mode in the runtime driver, or a
      service-kind branch in `_runtime_command`) that the persistent-service
      oracle uses, and keep the one-shot smoke mode for portable-application
      execution. Fail closed if a service artifact does not bind/serve.
- **Depends on:** [ACCEPTANCE-SERVICE-001](#acceptance-service-001-persistent-service-acceptance-oracle-never-runs-silent-false-pass)
      (#213, the routing fix — landed)
- **Root cause & fix (2026-09-01):** the only defect was the launch mode.
      `_accept_persistent_service` already launches the artifact as a detached,
      pollable `subprocess.Popen`; it just launched `_packaged_argv(EXECUTE)`
      which ends in `--litai-smoke` (one-shot). Added a `--litai-serve` mode:
      framework-owned mode-flag constants (`LITAI_TEST/SMOKE/SERVE_MODE_FLAG` in
      `contracts/components.py`), a `_packaged_service_argv` that swaps the
      trailing `--litai-smoke` for `--litai-serve` (fails closed if the EXECUTE
      argv does not end in the smoke sentinel), and `_accept_persistent_service`
      now launches that. The Node/native runtime drivers switched from blocking
      capture (`spawnSync` / `subprocess.run(capture_output=True)`) to streaming
      inherited stdio so a served process stays attached and pollable while the
      parent polls `/health` and then terminates it; one-shot smoke/test output
      semantics are preserved. The `python-service-application` and
      `rust-service-application` skills (catalog + init-template copies,
      byte-identical) now mandate the artifact recognize `--litai-serve` (bind
      host/port, serve, stay alive, expose `GET /health`). Fails closed when a
      service does not bind/serve.
- **Evidence:**
  - [x] The persistent-service launch command uses `--litai-serve`, not
        `--litai-smoke`; portable-application EXECUTE stays one-shot smoke.
        `tests/unit/test_service_package_entrypoint.py`
        (`RuntimeCommandModeTests`, `PackagedServiceArgvTests`) and the
        end-to-end `test_persistent_service_acceptance_runs_http_and_sse_and_stops`
        (forced live on darwin) pass — full launch→readiness→requests→shutdown.
        104 focused tests pass; `make skills-check` passes both service skills.
  - [ ] Live confirmation that a *generated* persistent-service artifact honors
        `--litai-serve` requires a live coding-CLI generation (downstream gate);
        the unit/e2e stubs prove the launch/oracle plumbing, not the generated
        artifact's `--litai-serve` implementation.

### [~] SPLIT-SERVICE-001 — First-class split web/API/collector/cache application pattern

- **Priority:** P1 (repeated real-world failure: generated single-service
      dashboards collect expensive upstream data in request handlers, lose all
      state on restart, and couple frontend deployment to credentials)
- **Release target:** 1.1.0
- **Previous release target:** 0.9.0 (feature; lands on `main`, ships in the minor)
- **GitHub issue:** [#216](https://github.com/NVIDIA-dev/literate-ai/issues/216)
      (concrete reusable application pattern; related to #33, #114, #115 but not
      just a generic multi-entrypoint mechanism or Component-kind taxonomy).
      Cross-layer lock-authority repair:
      [#243](https://github.com/NVIDIA-dev/literate-ai/issues/243).
- **Owning ADR:** [ADR 0027](../decisions/0027-durable-split-service-pattern.md)
      (Accepted 2026-09-01 after planning-cycle review; implementation scheduled)
- **Owner:** a portfolio sample + inheritable reference Component set (or exact
      specification-to-source guidance) for a four-boundary durable service,
      composed through public capability contracts.
- **Direction:** Two independent derived services (`portfolio-dashboard`,
      `telemetry-dashboard`) converged on the same provider-neutral architecture —
      browser frontend, read-only HTTP API, single-writer scheduled collector,
      and a durable embedded snapshot cache — that must be independently
      generated, deployed, restarted, and evidenced. Projects can model this
      manually today with multiple Components and `provides`/`requires`, but the
      reusable contracts are not cataloged, so generation repeatedly produces a
      single service that recollects upstream data in request handlers and loses
      availability on restart/failure. Catalog: (1) a browser frontend that
      consumes only a same-origin/read-only API; (2) a read-only API that
      consumes only a durable local snapshot store; (3) a single-writer
      collector/worker that alone may call upstream providers; (4) an embedded
      SQL snapshot cache (initially SQLite: WAL, busy timeout, migrations,
      read-only connections); plus capability contracts connecting the four
      without exposing private transitive specifications, independent entrypoints
      / deployment units, coherent current-snapshot publication after all
      required writes validate, and shared progress/freshness metadata. Keep
      provider commands, product schemas, credentials, and application vocabulary
      out of the framework template.
- **Depends on:** MULTI-ENTRYPOINT-001 (#33) — the multi-entrypoint / independent
      deployment-unit composition this pattern is built on (landed c02c2497).
- **Completed repair:** Centralize the planner-supported
      `component://…::+selector` grammar and replay each scoped selector only against
      its named lock node. The locked-generation verifier now preserves the planner's
      successful heterogeneous lock through source generation (#243).
- **Progress (2026-09-02):** framework parts landed. New leaf skill
      `backend-application/durable-split-service` (both copies byte-identical,
      pins the parent digest with no cascade) catalogs the four-boundary
      composition through public capabilities and references
      `frontend-application` + `scheduler-lease-worker` (#217) for those
      boundaries. Reference `tests/support/snapshot_cache_reference.py` proves the
      coherent-snapshot contract offline. The operator has now explicitly
      authorized live generation/build/execution and confirmed the local Cursor
      CLI is authenticated (`--yolo` for unattended execution). The live
      four-Component portfolio now passes generation, independent execution, browser,
      persistence, retry, lease, lock, and SBOM verification on macOS. Do not collapse
      the four authority boundaries into one
      multi-entrypoint Component: ADR 0026 supplies truthful deployment-unit
      evidence, while ADR 0027 deliberately keeps credentials and private source
      authority in separate Components.
- **Evidence:**
  - [x] A live-generated portfolio composes four Components through public
        capabilities and two independent Standard lifecycle roots.
  - [x] The collector is the only Component whose generated code can invoke the
        upstream fixture; API/frontend restart and failure paths make no upstream
        request.
  - [x] Restarting API and frontend serves a previously persisted snapshot
        without invoking the collector
        (`test_restart_reader_serves_persisted_snapshot_without_collector`).
  - [x] A failed partial write leaves readers on the prior complete snapshot
        (`test_aborted_partial_write_leaves_prior_snapshot`,
        `test_publish_missing_required_write_fails_and_keeps_prior`).
  - [x] Component locks and CycloneDX evidence preserve the exact four-boundary
        composition across five nested lifecycle nodes.
  - [ ] Generated and independent tests run on macOS, Linux, and Windows where
        SQLite is available (reference tests are portable; the generated matrix
        needs the live sample).
  - [x] Reader restart, partial-write failure, concurrent collector lease,
        expired-lease recovery, bounded retry, freshness/progress, and
        collector-only upstream access pass as externally meaningful flows in
        the generated portfolio.

### [ ] ACCEPTANCE-SERVICE-001 — Persistent-service acceptance oracle never runs (silent false-pass)

- **Priority:** P0 (silent false-pass on a service's behavioral/auth acceptance)
- **Release target:** 1.1.0
- **Previous release target:** 0.8.0 — release blocker. Not a CI blocker, but shipping
      0.8.0 with a silent false-pass on service acceptance is unacceptable; the
      cut waits on this fix.
- **GitHub issue:** [#213](https://github.com/NVIDIA-dev/literate-ai/issues/213)
- **Owner:** `src/literate_ai/adapters/lifecycle/standard_local.py` (project
      package plan entrypoint-kind), independent-acceptance routing
- **Direction:** A Component declaring a `persistent-service` entrypoint plus a
      `literate-ai/persistent-service-acceptance@1` oracle builds and reports
      `passed: true`, but the oracle never runs — the package plan hard-codes the
      entrypoint kind to `application`, so acceptance falls through to the
      `independent-acceptance-exempt@1` path. A generated artifact that is not
      even an HTTP server passes. `litai rebuild` reports a passing receipt for a
      service whose readiness/auth contract was never evaluated.
- **Conclusion:** The package plan must carry the Component's real entrypoint
      kind so `persistent-service` routes to the persistent-service acceptance
      oracle (reserve port, start artifact, poll `/health`, assert requests)
      instead of the exempt path. Do not weaken acceptance; fail closed when a
      declared service oracle cannot run. Needs a fix + regression proving a
      non-listening artifact fails the service oracle.

      scoping) — this is the service-kind counterpart that was left hard-coded.

      assignment; thread the real kind through; route persistent-service to its
      oracle; add a regression where a request-handler-only artifact (no listener)
      fails the service oracle instead of silently passing.
- **Root cause & fix (2026-08-31):** `LocalStandardLifecyclePorts.create_project_package`
      hard-coded `PackageEntrypoint("application", "application", ...)`, discarding
      the Component's declared kind. `accept_project_independently` and
      `execute_packaged_project` already route `persistent-service` correctly —
      the only defect was the hard-coded kind at package creation. Added
      `_root_package_entrypoint(component_lock)` which reads the root node's
      `definition.entrypoints[0]` `(name, kind)` and threads the real kind into
      the package plan. A Component with no/synthetic entrypoint keeps
      `application`.

        preserves `portable-application`; falls back to `application` for

        (4 tests).

### [ ] CI-FAILFAST-001 — Make pipeline fail-fast cancellation a first-class citizen

- **Clean-run repair (2026-09-16 UTC):** Probe-free run
      [35055235524](https://github.com/NVIDIA-dev/literate-ai/actions/runs/35055235524)
      passed two cells, then macOS sample composition failed because the nested
      model-routing Component change retained its previous harness authoring pin.
      Refreshed the reviewed sample authoring and specification identities; the
      execution-interface and independent oracle identities remain current. The
      exact hosted composition command now passes all 47 tests locally in 51.450
      seconds. Fresh hosted qualification is still required. The cancelled cells
      are not passes; this item remains open.

- **Implemented cancellation scope:** Consolidate the existing fifteen skill,
      documentation, composition, Linux/macOS conformance and Windows gate/test
      cells into one native `fail-fast: true` matrix. Preserve each published check
      name, platform/Python selection, command, action pin, artifact and status-aware
      cleanup step; retain run concurrency cancellation and read-only permissions.
      Compare each selected cell with its original execution plan, validate Actions
      syntax and retain real hosted cancellation evidence before closing this item.

- **Release target:** 1.1.0

- **Priority:** P1 (runner-resource waste)
- **Owner:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, release-gate CI orchestration
- **Direction:** User-directed: CI wastes a large amount of GitHub runner time
      because every matrix job declared `fail-fast: false`, so all OS/Python
      combinations run to completion even after one host has already failed.
      A change that fails on one host is going to fail the run regardless; we
      should stop the rest immediately.
- **Conclusion:** Two levels of cancellation:
  1. Within each matrix — flipped `fail-fast: false` → `fail-fast: true` on all
     four matrix jobs (documentation, sample-composition, the Python matrix, and
     the Windows job) so a failing cell cancels its siblings. Done in this item.
  2. Across independent top-level jobs — GitHub Actions does not natively
     fail-fast across separate jobs. Design a cross-job cancellation mechanism:
     a fast "gate" job (lint/format/quick unit subset) that the heavy jobs
     `needs:`, or a reusable-workflow/step-level cancellation so a failure in any
     platform cancels the others in the same run. This preserves the ability to
     see a single authoritative failure while not paying for the full matrix on a
     known-bad change.
- **Depends on:** none
- **Implementation:**
  - [x] Flip `fail-fast: false` → `true` on every matrix in `ci.yml`.
  - [x] Put all fifteen required checks in one native fail-fast matrix so a
        failure in any platform or task cancels unfinished siblings across the
        previous top-level job boundaries. Job-level continuation is false; no
        token-write permission or cancellation service is needed.
  - [x] Keep `concurrency.cancel-in-progress: true` (already set) so a new push
        cancels the previous run.
- **Evidence:**
  - [x] A push whose change fails on one platform cancels the remaining matrix
        cells instead of running the full matrix to completion: hosted run
        [35055053274](https://github.com/NVIDIA-dev/literate-ai/actions/runs/35055053274)
        at `40fa0bf75c5a7975cd3f63341c2dfdce84f551fe` deliberately failed only
        Ubuntu documentation and cancelled all fourteen other cells across Linux,
        macOS and Windows. All fifteen cells reached terminal states before any
        subsequent push; no manual workflow cancellation was used.
  - [ ] The probe-free final head passes the complete hosted matrix before landing.

- **Local validation:** All 30 CI action-pin, impact and planning tests pass.
      A parsed before/after comparison proves every original step and parameter in
      all fifteen selected cells is preserved, including status-aware evidence
      uploads and failure explanations. Actionlint 1.7.12 validates the resulting
      workflow (external shellcheck/Pyflakes disabled); original command bodies are
      byte-preserved. Retained records: `_build/ci-projection-evidence.json`,
      `_build/ci-failfast-tests.log` and `_build/ci-actionlint.log`.
- **Hosted evidence:** Draft [PR #441](https://github.com/NVIDIA-dev/literate-ai/pull/441)
      is stacked on #438. The first head could not start CI because review pins

      only the evidence ledger. Reuse the existing release-file custody validator;
      do not rebuild an allegedly equivalent wheel for upload or treat CI artifacts
      as publication approval. Historical published-wheel proof remains separate.
      Local custody and existing wheel-smoke unit suites pass (17 tests), including
      changed input/copy refusals, independent repeat custody and linked output
      refusal. Fresh installed-wheel and hosted upload evidence remain outstanding.

        GitHub Release as an asset.
  - [ ] Verify the published wheel installs cleanly and `litai version check`
        reports the tagged version.

## Detailed-roadmap lifecycle

This file is the sole resumable queue. Create a supporting document beneath
`docs/roadmap/` only when a program's rationale, ordering, and acceptance contract no
longer fit one queue item without obscuring its next action. Every such document must
place these visible fields between its title and first section:

```markdown
- **Status:** active
- **Owning queue item:** [AREA-NNN](active-work.md#area-nnn-heading)
- **Completion / archival evidence:** pending while AREA-NNN remains open
```

The allowed states are:

- `active`: selected by its owning queue item and presently executable;
- `partial`: durable milestones have landed but its complete acceptance contract has not;
- `deferred`: deliberately ineligible until the header names the prerequisite or decision;
- `completed`: all acceptance evidence is linked in the header; and
- `historical`: terminal documentation moved beneath `docs/history/roadmap/`, with its
  original owner and archival evidence retained.

`Owning queue item` must link to an existing checkbox heading or named program heading
in this file. A completed plan may remain beneath `docs/roadmap/` when marking it
`completed` preserves useful inbound links; substantial closed programs should move to
the history area and use `historical`. A terminal state without linked evidence is
invalid. Ordinary queue items do not gain separate files merely to satisfy this header.

**Upstream compatibility review:** All four proposed full commit pins resolve to
their named upstream release tags. The existing workflow uses GitHub-hosted
Linux/macOS/Windows runners, explicit Python/Node selections and read-only
repository permissions. The action runtime's Node 24 runner floor is inherited
from the already selected generations; it is not a new project runtime floor.

- [Checkout v7](https://github.com/actions/checkout/releases/tag/v7.0.0) blocks
  unsafe fork checkouts on privileged `pull_request_target`/`workflow_run` events;
  this workflow uses neither event. Preserve that protection without an opt-out.
- [Setup-python v7](https://github.com/actions/setup-python/releases/tag/v7.0.0)
  removes `pip-install` and migrates internals to ESM; the workflow does not use
  that removed input. [Setup-node v7](https://github.com/actions/setup-node/releases/tag/v7.0.0)
  also migrates to ESM; preserve explicit `package-manager-cache: false` and
  the existing Node 24 selection.
- [Setup-uv v8](https://github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/releases/tag/v8.0.0) changes
  custom manifest format and removes floating major/minor tags; neither is used.
  [v9](https://github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/releases/tag/v9.0.0) changes default
  cache pruning, and [v10](https://github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/releases/tag/v10.0.0)
  changes caching for sensitive events and adds a checksum-known version selector.
  Review cache policy explicitly and bind the installed uv version when integrating.

**Non-vacuous qualification requirement:** The setup-uv step is conditional on
changed skills. A workflow-only bump has none, so its green admission job can
skip the very action being upgraded. Add an always-exercised, version-bound uv
bootstrap check while retaining conditional skill evaluation, and require that
actual step plus the combined platform matrix to pass before #383 closes.

addition to their included disposition and matching milestone; this classification
is not approval of the dependency changes.

wheel `literate_ai-0.8.1-py3-none-any.whl` attached; `verify-published` ok. The
0.8.1 patch fixes the 0.8.0 Windows known issue. The "manifest lock failed" was
actually `os.fsync` on a directory handle in `_replace` (Windows rejects
`FlushFileBuffers` on a directory), guarded to POSIX; plus lock-primitive
convergence on the proven `_cache_lock` path, a Windows delete-pending `EACCES`
retry on concurrent lock-file open, DOC-IDENTITY advisory `.as_posix()`, and an
idempotent `gh release upload --clobber` (RELEASE-018-IDEMPOTENT). **Windows CI
is now green** on both `main` and `release/0.8.x`. The five fixes landed on
`main` first then cherry-picked to the release line; the `LITAI_LOCK_DIAG`
diagnostic and its CI env var were removed once green. WINDOWS-LOCK-001 and
RELEASE-018-IDEMPOTENT are closed.

## 0.4.0 planning — filed GitHub issues

Downstream 0.3.0 usage on real multi-surface Components (HTTP API + MCP server +
scheduled worker + web dashboard), plus a separate Physics Workbench sample native-qualification
effort, surfaced the issues below, all filed against the installed
`literate-ai==0.3.0` launcher. None blocked the 0.3.0 cut; they became the planning
queue for the next release. Originally scoped as a 0.3.1 patch, retargeted to 0.4.0
once the batch's own scope made clear it carries real new capabilities (configurable
provider selection, timeout, priority order; provider-resolution and inherited-session
contracts; concurrent target matrices; a per-worker SSH transport), not just bug
fixes — a SemVer minor bump, not a patch. Plus one filed mid-pass from live
target-matrix testing (#65). On
2026-08-15 the queue was worked end to end: 9 issues fixed and merged to `main` (#31,
#33, #34, #46, #54, #55, #57, #61, #63), 2 closed as won't-fix (#51, #52 — see below),
5 open PRs (#37/#62, #41/#48, #42/#50, #43/#49, and the CI-repair branch that became
#60) synced with `main` and merged or pending green CI, #65 partially fixed (verifier
diagnostics, per-worker SSH transport) with the remote-continuation gap precisely
root-caused and deferred, and the remainder (#32, #35, #36, #39, #56, #58, #64)
investigated and explicitly deferred with reasoning rather than rushed.

### [ ] STANDARD-PROJECT-REBUILD-001 — Standard rebuild of the project root rebuilds every locked Component

- **Release target:** 1.1.0
- **Integration repair (locally verified):** PR #447 executed every selected root but published only the last Component's finalized receipt. The repaired root path now combines typed accepted candidates, binds the full canonical lock set and every member proof, and publishes matching CLI/candidate/committed receipt identities and totals. It captures initial project authority and rechecks configuration, every input snapshot, the driver and lock-set membership before publication. Missing, duplicate, foreign or stale members refuse publication. Single-Component receipt identities remain unchanged; per-Component results retain their complete product metadata. This owner remains open for final qualification.
- **Priority:** high
- **Owner:** src/literate_ai/cli/rebuild.py Standard rebuild entry
- **GitHub issue:** [#445](https://github.com/NVIDIA-dev/literate-ai/issues/445)
- **Direction:** litai rebuild . on a Standard-bound project must rebuild every Component with a committed lock instead of failing closed with rebuild.standard_component_required.
- **Conclusion:** Keep one-Component rebuild unchanged. Project-root Standard rebuild enumerates the current lock set, runs each lifecycle under one project lock, fails closed before receipt commit if any Component fails, and returns an aggregated DAG and test summary. Unlocked catalog entries remain skipped.
- **Depends on:** MULTI-ENTRYPOINT-001

### [~] TOOLING-001 — A green `litai build`/test-suite is not evidence the implementation is complete

- **Release target:** 1.1.0

- **Priority:** P1
- **GitHub issue:** [#64](https://github.com/NVIDIA-dev/literate-ai/issues/64)
- **Owner:** independent-acceptance / test-generation coverage signal (not yet a single
  owning module)
- **Direction:** The same coding-CLI call that writes a Component's implementation also
  writes its own test suite, so the tests can only ever exercise whatever surface that
  call decided to implement — a generated API Component shipped with several route
  handlers literally set to `None` despite 17/17 generated tests passing; a generated
  worker Component never called its own upstream client despite 15/15 passing. Neither
  gap was caught by build/test/acceptance, only by running the application end to end.
- **Conclusion:** This is a process/tooling gap, not a single bug with one fix shape —
  it needs an independent signal, distinct from the acceptance-oracle smoke test
  (#32/ACCEPTANCE-001), that measures how much of the specification's described
  behavior the generated tests actually exercise. Filed here as a problem statement
  and direction, not implemented; needs its own design pass to pick a concrete
  coverage-signal mechanism before scoping further.
- **Superseded 2026-08-16 by COVERAGE-GAP-001** (below): landed a first, narrow,
  advisory-only mechanical scan (whole-generated-tree stub-marker detection). Left
  marked partial `[~]` here, not `[x]`, because the fail-closed direction this entry
  originally called for ("fails some lifecycle phase before acceptance") was
  explicitly deferred — see COVERAGE-GAP-001 for the actual landed scope and its
  precision-tradeoff reasoning.
- **Evidence:**
  - [ ] A generated Component with an unimplemented declared surface (e.g. a `None`
        route handler) fails some lifecycle phase before acceptance, not just at
        manual end-to-end review.

### [ ] WORKER-006 — Keep remote accepted-source keys below host path limits

- **Release target:** 1.1.0
- **Previous release target:** 0.9.0 (re-scoped 2026-09-01: had no explicit target)
- **Priority:** P0
- **GitHub issue:** [#101](https://github.com/NVIDIA-dev/literate-ai/issues/101)
- **Owner:** bounded remote source materialization and worker lifecycle cache custody
- **Direction:** Physics Workbench sample regenerated and admitted exactly twelve current Windows source
  memberships, but cache-only restore could not open an archived key membership beneath
  the request checkout. The failing native path was exactly 260 characters; archive
  identity, staging, exact launcher selection, and fail-closed generator suppression had
  already passed.
- **Conclusion:** The accepted-source archive is portable, but restoring its
  content-addressed key hierarchy below the arbitrarily long request checkout reintroduces
  a host path-length dependency. Restore each request into a short, attempt-scoped build
  root, bind that root as explicit lifecycle custody from worker transport through
  rebuild and accepted-source lookup, and remove it after success or failure. Preserve
  key and membership identities unchanged; do not special-case any observed digest,
  weaken archive verification, or fall back to generation.
- **Regression after PR #103:** Real Physics Workbench sample validation against merged parent
  `a1acacbb4458734950486009ac42235aaa8049c5` proved archive staging and the short
  archive contract succeed, but still reported a 260-character request-checkout cache
  path and failed `cli.invalid_input`. The run admitted twelve Windows memberships,
  passed all 36 generated tests, selected no coding CLI, and leaked no short-cache
  directory. This is distinct from #104's Linux semantic-key absence.
- **Root cause after PR #107:** An in-band native-path trace against merged parent
  `3c1e5fc7873ab9af24b4f950c3ae32bd335cc0d8` located the failing write in

  identity-bound cache archive. Windows therefore tried to materialize the duplicate
  key below the long request checkout before PR #107's short custody could run.

### [ ] SPEC-REFINEMENT-001 — Refine abstract requests into sufficient Component authority

- **Release target:** 1.1.0
- **Previous release target:** 0.9.0 (re-scoped 2026-09-01: had no explicit target)
- **Priority:** P1
- **Owner:** framework core / specification authoring and review
- **Direction:** A user should be able to begin with a mission-level request that mixes
  simple application surfaces, complex computation, deployment topology, and host-bound
  measurement without already knowing Literate AI's Component, specification-provider,
  Flavor, skill, or acceptance taxonomy. The framework must explain which decisions are
  still missing, propose the narrowest appropriate authority for each concern, and stop
  before generation whenever an independent verifier could not decide correctness from
  the resulting authority alone.
- **Conclusion:** [ADR 0013](../decisions/0013-intent-refinement-and-specification-sufficiency.md)
  defines an intent-refinement phase before lock and plan. Refinement produces a
  non-authoritative design draft: a proposed Component graph, concern classifications,
  assumptions and defaults, blocking questions, target-bound selections, acceptance
  obligations, and per-Component sufficiency findings. Specification depth is selected
  per concern rather than assigned once to a whole project. Only explicit user review
  may materialize the draft as authored Component, interface, Flavor-selection, asset,
  and acceptance authority; structural validation, model confidence, compilation, and
  generated tests are not substitutes. The ADR uses a distributed CPU/GPU pi service
  with an HTTP API, streamed progress, host resource accounting, and web frontend as the
  reference decomposition and recommends it as a bounded future sample after the core
  refinement contract exists.
- **Dependencies:** Define provider-neutral refinement contracts and the acceptance-
  decidability policy first; add preview/explain/accept application services and CLI
  adapters second; add the bounded pi-service sample only after those contracts can
  drive its authoring flow without sample-specific logic.
- **Next action:** Design the versioned `IntentRefinementRequest`, `DesignDraft`, concern,
  question, decision, and sufficiency-finding wire contracts plus their deterministic
  validation rules. Do not implement generation or the pi-service sample first.
        **In progress 2026-08-28:** contracts and `litai design` landed; ADR 0013 remains
        Proposed; the bounded pi-service sample is still gated.
- **Evidence:**
  - [x] ADR 0013 records the decision, authority boundary, sufficiency rule, concern
        taxonomy, refinement lifecycle, proposed CLI/report shape, and pi-service
        reference decomposition.
  - [x] Versioned provider-neutral refinement and sufficiency contracts have strict
        schemas, canonical identities, bounded fields, and round-trip tests.
  - [x] `litai design refine`, `litai design explain`, and `litai design accept` (or a
        reviewed equivalent surface) preserve draft authority, expose every blocking
        question, and materialize accepted authoring atomically without invoking
        generation.
        Accept records a receipt only; it does not write `component.md`.
  - [x] Conformance fixtures prove simple requests remain one Component, mixed-depth
        requests select authority per concern, unanswered blocking questions prevent
        acceptance, and target-bound CPU/GPU choices remain outside portable behavior.
  - [ ] The bounded pi-service sample generates, builds, and independently verifies its
        numerical, streaming, measurement, and multi-Component contracts on declared
        CPU and optional accelerator targets without embedding host APIs in the portable
        computation specification.

### [~] FLAVOR-ZIG-001 — Add Zig language and Zig-backed C/C++ cross-compilation

- **Release target:** 1.1.0

- **Priority:** P1
- **Owner:** Flavor catalog, toolchain resolution, builders, and specification-to-source
  skills
- **Direction:** Add Zig as a first-class implementation language and use Zig's bundled
  Clang/LLD/libc cross toolchain as the preferred portable realization when a Component
  explicitly requires cross-architecture or cross-OS compilation. Preserve the semantic
  difference between generating Zig source and compiling existing C/C++ source through
  `zig cc` or `zig c++`; never relabel C/C++ authority as Zig merely because Zig drives
  compilation.
- **Conclusion:** [ADR 0014](../decisions/0014-zig-language-and-c-cpp-cross-compilation.md)
  defines two composable authorities: `lang-zig` on the language axis and
  `toolchain-zig-cc` on the toolchain axis. An explicit cross-compilation requirement
  raises Zig above native C/C++ toolchains when the required target is supported. For a
  greenfield Component that permits language substitution, policy may prefer `lang-zig`
  over C/C++; for authored or generated C/C++ source, it retains `lang-c`/`lang-cpp` and
  selects `toolchain-zig-cc`. Native builds do not silently change, and unsupported
  target/libc/ABI combinations fail during planning rather than falling back to the host.
- **Dependencies:** Canonical Flavor naming from ADR 0010; target profiles that bind OS,
  architecture, ABI/libc, and minimum deployment compatibility; current exact toolchain
  discovery and build authorization.
- **Next action:** Standard host adapter for `zig` and `zig-cc` landed as
  `57d165dd` (isolated `931b57f5`). Remaining: a live `zig` compile and a
  portfolio sample (same dormant pattern as Swift until a real binary can
  compile). Do not fake a compile.
- **Evidence:**
  - [x] ADR 0014 records the language/toolchain split, preference policy, target model,
        build and package rules, security boundary, compatibility behavior, and complete
        Flavor/skill acceptance requirements.
  - [x] `lang-zig` and `toolchain-zig-cc` catalog independently (empty `conflicts:` both
        ways; distinct slots `zig` vs `zig-cc`). `_discover_toolchain` now admits `zig`
        and `zig-cc`: runs `zig version`, binds launcher bytes, keeps `cc`/`c++` as
        argv, fail-closes with `https://ziglang.org/download/` when missing.
        `tests.unit.test_zig_toolchain` 15/15 with fakes. No live `zig` on the host;
        no compile was faked.
  - [ ] A native Zig Component and C and C++ Components cross-compiled through `zig cc`
        and `zig c++` generate, build, test, inspect, and run on declared destination
        targets; no test executes a foreign artifact on the build host.
  - [ ] Selection tests prove explicit cross-compilation prefers Zig where supported,
        native compilation remains unchanged without that requirement, explicit user
        selections win, and unsupported ABI/libc/sysroot combinations fail closed.
  - [ ] The Zig and Zig C/C++ skills pass the pinned SkillEvaluator gate, and installed-
        project plus cross-platform CI prove template/catalog parity.

### [ ] WORKER-007 — Preserve cross-platform SSH command and result contracts

- **Release target:** 1.1.0

- **Priority:** P0
- **GitHub issues:** [#126](https://github.com/NVIDIA-dev/literate-ai/issues/126),
  [#127](https://github.com/NVIDIA-dev/literate-ai/issues/127)
- **Owner:** bounded SSH lifecycle transport and remote execution result projection
- **Direction:** Final-distribution cross-platform qualification found that Windows SSH
  commands are unconditionally wrapped in `bash -lic` before their PowerShell receiver,
  while a Linux accepted-source lifecycle completes build, tests, smoke execution, and
  indexing but is rejected while projecting its typed remote result.
- **Conclusion:** Select the remote shell from explicit worker OS authority without
  requiring a POSIX shell on Windows, and preserve every successful worker lifecycle as
  a valid `ExecutionDispatchResult`. Keep SSH verification, deadlines, output bounds,
  exact source custody, and generator suppression unchanged. Typed diagnostics must name
  the invalid contract field rather than collapse successful work to an opaque error.
- **Depends on:** merged accepted-source transport and short-root custody through
  `7ea71af66c6687da1c0d6e7223c1f61d028ca5c6`
- **Root cause:** SSH transport always imposed `bash -lic` even though the lifecycle
  adapter had already selected a PowerShell receiver for Windows. On Linux, the hardware
  probe correctly reported `NVIDIA RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell Generation`, but projection
  into `ObservedExecutionEnvironment` reused the narrower portable-scalar validator,
  which rejects spaces, after the lifecycle had completed.
- **Implementation:**
  - [x] Make SSH remote-shell projection OS-aware for setup, execute, and cleanup while
        retaining per-worker transport-binary authority.
  - [x] Repair the post-lifecycle Linux result contract and preserve precise bounded
        validation diagnostics.
  - [x] Add Windows-without-Bash and GPU-observed successful-build regressions.
- **Evidence:**
  - [x] Focused SSH transport, remote execution, contract, and worker CLI regressions
        pass within the clean 2,436-test Python suite (28 platform skips).
  - [ ] Full cross-platform CI passes, followed by real Linux and Windows accepted-source
        worker qualification with no coding-provider fallback.

### [ ] PROC-KILL-001 — Windows process-tree kill misses late-spawned grandchildren

- **Priority:** P0
- **Release target:** 1.1.0
- **Previous release target:** 0.7.3 remaining in-package call sites. The Job Object
  primitive, `run_with_tree_kill`, and dispatcher bind shipped on this line
  before `v0.7.2`; several timeout `Popen` sites still omit `ownership`.
- **Re-scoped:** 0.9.0 (2026-09-01) for any remaining work; the historical target above records where the item originated / partially shipped.
- **GitHub issue:** [#72](https://github.com/NVIDIA-dev/literate-ai/issues/72)
- **Owner:** `src/literate_ai/adapters/_processes.py` —
  `process_group_options`/`terminate_process_tree`
- **Direction:** Windows `CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP` only affects console `CTRL_BREAK`
  routing; it is not `killpg`-equivalent. Tree kill is a separate `taskkill /T` snapshot,
  and a grandchild that spawns after that snapshot (or when `taskkill` is skipped, e.g. a
  sanitized environment missing `SystemRoot`) survives a supposed timeout-kill. The
  surviving descendant keeps the parent's inherited PIPE write ends open (hang / false
  `output_stream` failure) or keeps a file handle open in a directory the caller expects
  to be free to delete (`PermissionError` on cleanup).
- **Reproduced live, independently, twice in one CI run (2026-08-16):** landing the
  CI-SHARD-001 Windows test-sharding split surfaced this exact bug class twice in a
  single run, in two different shards, via two different symptoms:
  - `tests/critical/test_authorized_host_execution.py::AuthorizedHostExecutionTests::test_timeout_kills_host_process_descendants`
    — the descendant's sentinel file existed after the timeout kill, meaning the
    descendant was never actually terminated.
  - `tests/conformance/test_self_hosting.py::SnapshotReplicationConformanceTests::test_isolated_candidate_timeout_terminates_descendant_process_tree`
    — `PermissionError: [WinError 32] The process cannot access the file because it is
    being used by another process`, cleaning up a temp directory a surviving descendant
    still held open.
  Both reruns passed on retry, consistent with a race rather than a deterministic
  failure — exactly the causal sequence #72 describes (grandchild spawn racing the
  `taskkill` snapshot).
- **Conclusion:** Assign the child to a Win32 Job Object with
  `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` so the OS itself guarantees every descendant dies
  when the job handle closes, keeping `taskkill` only as a fallback for hosts where Job
  Objects are unavailable. Never treat `CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP` as a process-group
  primitive on Windows.
- **Implementation:**
  - [x] Add Win32 Job Object assignment (`CreateJobObjectW` +
        `SetInformationJobObject(JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE)` +
        `AssignProcessToJobObject`) in `_processes.py`
        (`create_process_tree_ownership` / `ProcessTreeOwnership.bind`).
  - [x] Keep `taskkill /T` as an explicit fallback path, not the primary
        mechanism, for hosts where Job Object creation fails closed.
  - [x] Add a regression that binds the root before a (simulated) late
        grandchild and kills the job when `taskkill` is unavailable
        (`test_process_tree_ownership_binds_before_grandchild_spawn`).
  - [x] Adopt `create_process_tree_ownership` + `bind` at remaining in-package
        timeout spawn sites that still pass only `process_group_options()` into
        `Popen` (builders, host execution, SSH, sandbox, coding CLI, harness,
        source-index, persistent-service). Standalone worker scripts stay
        stdlib-only and keep validated `taskkill`.
  - [x] Route remaining in-package Git `subprocess.run(timeout=)` sites
        (parent checkout, tracker inspect, source capture) through
        `run_with_tree_kill` so late Git/SSH helpers join the same Job Object
        / process-group kill as the Popen sites. Do this on `main` / 0.8.0;
        do not merge `release/0.7.x` or cut RELEASE-013 here.
        Parent checkout uses `run_bounded_process` (reap then tree-kill) so
        lingering pipe holders are not mistaken for a hung `communicate()`.
        Other Git `timeout=` sites remain in init origin lookup, user-config
        HEAD, source-index, and release Git helpers.
- **Evidence:**
  - [x] Fake-kernel32 regression: bind-before-grandchild, abandon-on-assign-
        failure, `KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` flag, POSIX has no job.
  - [x] Remaining in-package spawn sites pass `ownership` into
        `terminate_process_tree`.
  - [ ] `test_timeout_kills_host_process_descendants` and
        `test_isolated_candidate_timeout_terminates_descendant_process_tree`
        remain the Windows CI canaries.

### [ ] FLAVOR-001 — Add `make` build-system Flavor with smart init defaults

- **Release target:** 1.1.0
- **Previous release target:** 0.9.0 (re-scoped 2026-09-01: had no explicit target)
- **Owner:** framework Flavor catalog (`flavors/make/`), init adapter, CLI
- **Direction (revised after evaluation):** Bazel is the right build system for
  literate-ai's own qualification samples (hermetic, reproducible) but is wrong as
  the *default* for new projects — it is not pre-installed on any OS and its
  installation burden fails the very first `litai rebuild` for a new user. Make is
  pre-installed on macOS, every Linux distro, and Git-for-Windows. Similarly, every
  project needs an implementation language; Python is the right default because it
  has a rich ecosystem, is available everywhere without a compiler toolchain, and is
  the natural choice for documentation projects (Sphinx), scripting, and data work.
  The host OS is always knowable at init time and should never require `--flavor`.
- **Decision (confirmed):**
  - `+make` replaces `+bazel` as the default `build.system` for `litai init`.
    Bazel remains available and explicitly selected by the framework's own sample
    projects.
  - `+python` is the default `implementation.language-ecosystem` when no language
    Flavor is declared. A project with no language is dubious even for documentation
    (Sphinx is Python).
  - The host OS (`+macos`, `+linux`, or `+windows`) is always auto-detected from
    `sys.platform` and never required via `--flavor`.
  - `--flavor` is now **optional** for `litai init`. With no flags, the project gets
    `["+python", "+make", "+<host-os>"]`. Explicit `--flavor` values override the
    relevant axis. Unknown explicit values still fail with the known-selector
    diagnostic.
  - literate-ai's own `default_flavor_selectors` changes from `+bazel` to `+make`
    because the framework builds with Make, not Bazel.
- **Depends on:** none
- **Implementation:**
  - [x] Create `flavors/make/flavor.md`, `standard-make-command-profile.json`, and
        `openspec/spec.md`. The dedicated Make profile names its exact generated
        Makefile and build target; it does not reuse the Bazel target-label schema.
  - [x] Implement typed native-Make Standard execution with exact GNU Make launcher,
        version, language-tool, output-custody, generated-test, execution, dependency,
        and drift evidence. Keep the existing Bazel profile and language-agnostic
        native adapter independent.
  - [x] Create `skills/specification-to-source/make-build-system/SKILL.md` with
        full contract frontmatter.
  - [x] Add Make to `_TEMPLATE_FILES`, `KNOWN_FLAVOR_SELECTORS`, `_FLAVOR_AXIS_DEFAULTS`.
  - [x] Add `host_platform_selector()` (public) to `project_initialization.py`.
  - [x] Add `_apply_init_flavor_defaults()` to `project.py`; remove the
        "require --flavor" error; `--flavor` is now optional.
  - [x] Change literate-ai `default_flavor_selectors`: `+bazel` → `+make`.
  - [x] Update tests: smart-default tests replace error-on-missing tests.
  - [x] Make the framework's own conformance sample catalog retain
        an explicit Bazel build selection instead of inheriting the new project-level
        Make default into samples whose executable harness remains Bazel-authored.
  - [x] Keep the repository skill catalog and initialized-project template copy of
        `make-build-system` byte-identical so `litai init` ships the current skill
        contract instead of an older duplicate.
- **Evidence:**
  - [x] `litai init` (no flags) → `["+python", "+make", "+<host-os>"]` in
        `literate.project.json`; only python + make + host-os Flavor files installed.
  - [x] `litai init --flavor javascript` → `["+javascript", "+make", "+<host-os>"]`
        (python not added; make fills uncovered build axis; OS auto-detected).
  - [x] `litai init --flavor javascript --flavor bazel` → `["+javascript", "+bazel",
        "+<host-os>"]` (no make; no python; user's explicit axes respected).
  - [x] Unknown `--flavor openscad` exits with `project.init_flavor_unknown`.
  - [x] 28 initialization adapter tests pass.
  - [ ] The focused sample-plan regression and a clean resumable `make release-check`
        pass from the repaired commit.
  - [x] Template-parity regression proves initialized projects receive
        `make-build-system` version 1.3.0, its root-level delegation contract, and the
